sampling_model.design: Independent replicate wells are collected at fixed, known integer composition rows of \(M\). The two-row matrix \(M_0\) is a synthetic prospective-design application.
sampling_model.units: A unit is one replicate well containing exactly the declared number of independent cells of each labeled type; rowwise random splitting produces \(N_A\) training wells and \(N_B\) inference wells, both split sizes diverge, and the row fractions converge to a normalized rational probability vector \(\rho\) that is strictly positive for every sampled composition row.
sampling_model.treatment: For \(p\geq3\), the ordered embedding \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\) is fixed before analysis. The interventions \(\operatorname{do}(V_{i_X}=1)\) and \(\operatorname{do}(V_{i_X}=2)\) are counterfactual count interventions, and responses are the coordinates \(V_{i_Y}\) and \(V_{i_Z}\), evaluated by truncated factorization after type-law and graph recovery.
sampling_model.overlap: Positive Poisson roots and rates give full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\), so the fixed parent configurations at the designated coordinates \(i_X,i_Y,i_Z\) are observationally supported within the benchmark family.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Pooled PGFs are empirical replicate-well averages; component PGFs use log inversion; graph and parameter estimates use the deterministic lexicographic sample-split selector; the certifier validates allocation normalization before covariance calculations, and inference is activated only by a certificate of positive sampled-row fractions, wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local nonsingularity, positive interiority clearance, and precision.

Theorems 1--2 identify component distributions up to shifts, and Section 4 estimates transform mixtures by GMM.
Theorem 2 obtains component recovery under pairwise column independence for a generalized-hyperexponential approximation class.
The paper uses causal minimality and pairwise identifiability to recover a CPCM DAG from its direct observational law while permitting arbitrary source-node laws.

Definition 3 specifies PT-SEM from direct observational count vectors; Theorem 12 identifies its DAG, thinning matrix, and node-wise exogenous distributions under (A1)--(A3), and Theorem 18 proves plug-in BIC selection consistency under (A1)--(A5).
Section 4.2 studies functional consistency under linear aggregation and gives affine ANM/PNL consequences; Section 4.3 concerns conditional-independence consistency.
The paper establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and covariance weighting for finite or continuum moments.
The article develops mathematically rigorous verification methods based on directed floating-point and interval arithmetic.
The article distinguishes rigorous from non-rigorous deterministic branch-and-bound and reviews sound interval relaxations and termination claims.
The paper combines Taylor-model enclosures with branch-and-bound for rigorous global search.
The paper constructs rigorous interval quasiconvex relaxations for self-validating constrained global optimization.
Theorems 2 and 4 certify approximate polynomial roots and common associated roots.
The paper optimizes network-tomography probe allocation using Fisher information.

body.tldr: Known linearly independent raw-count compositions recover unrestricted labeled type laws for arbitrary \(p\geq1\) by a logarithmic count-PGF inverse that draws on Shih--Hero's independent-additive transform-inversion idea, with positive Poisson aliases proving necessity. For \(p\geq3\), a fixed ordered embedding defines one exposure and two responses. The headline finite-input certifier constructs and verifies a rational chart-projection cover and separately proves wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local Jacobian nonsingularity, interiority clearance, PGF-tail control, and designated-contrast precision. Its deterministic selector supports pointwise sample-split Wald inference. The design frontier is finite under explicit caps, and the fully specified three-node input is a synthetic prospective benchmark with exactly one allowed refinement.

project_justification.gap: Transform inversion, direct-law CPCM and Poisson-thinning DAG identification, and validated numerics are established separately, but no result recovers labeled type laws through known multi-composition pools and propagates infinite-support PGF tails through distinct wrong-graph, global within-graph, local-regularity, and causal-precision certificates.
project_justification.niche: Prospective known-composition designs need a proof-producing decision rule whose global identification, local inference, and measurable selection premises are exactly declared.
project_justification.fill: The project combines the arbitrary-dimensional rank frontier with a finite \(p\geq3\) certifier that constructs and verifies a rational chart-projection cover, a deterministic estimator, an arithmetic ceiling, and a finite Pareto design class.

body.related_work: Shih--Hero is credited at the source-verified level for transform inversion of independent additive link delays; no unavailable primary-source equation or rank premise is attributed to it. The displayed count-PGF inverse and the positive unrestricted converse are derived in the rank theorem. Chen--Cao--Bu and Thoppe inform transform estimation and restricted tomography identification. Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin, Definition 10 and Lemma 11, supplies pairwise identifiability and recovery of a causally minimal CPCM DAG from its direct law. Its CPCM framework permits arbitrary source-node laws; Poisson roots and positive-polynomial non-root kernels are stricter conditions maintained by this paper. Gao--Cai--Hara, Definition 3, Proposition 10, Theorem 12, and Theorem 18, identifies a Poisson-thinning DAG, thinning coefficients, and exogenous laws from the direct observational count law and gives consistent plug-in BIC selection; its input is not a collection of known multi-composition pools, and it supplies neither labeled type-law unpooling nor a joint PGF-tail, graph-gap, global-injectivity, and causal-precision certificate. Luo--Sun--Zhang Section 4.2 studies functional consistency under linear aggregation and gives affine ANM/PNL consequences; Section 4.3 concerns conditional-independence consistency. Known labeled multi-composition pools remain outside its target. These results motivate prospective auxiliary composition information rather than a claim that all recoverability is restricted to linear aggregation or a claim about normalized legacy bulk data. Carrasco--Florens and Newey--McFadden inform minimum distance, global extremum identification, measurable selection, and delta inference. Rump, Sections 2--4 and 10, supplies directed rounding and verified linear algebra; Kearfott supplies rigorous global-optimization semantics; Berz--Makino and Jansson supply validated Taylor and interval relaxations. Hauenstein--Sottile informs local root checks but not compact analytic image exclusion. The new ingredient is joint propagation of analytic Poisson-PGF tails through wrong-graph exclusion, a verified chart-projection cover, remote within-graph separation, local singular values, pooled covariance, and designated causal precision.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The \(27\)-point floating-point pilot is not a certificate. Its two local Jacobian singular values are approximately \(0.00326480\) and \(0.00262027\), but it checks neither global within-graph uniqueness nor every wrong-graph box, tail error, or rigorous precision. The reusable procedure may return \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\) or certify an obstruction.
body.honest_scope: Unrestricted rank recovery and stability apply for arbitrary \(p\geq1\). Causal transfer, certification, benchmark contrasts, precision, and Wald inference require \(p\geq3\) and the same explicit ordered embedding \(\iota\); covariance and Wald claims additionally use a normalized allocation with strictly positive fractions for every sampled composition row. Global injectivity is certified by local chart monotonicity plus remote pair separation, never inferred from a positive Jacobian singular value; singleton candidate classes and empty remote-pair sets use the explicit \(+\infty\) convention. The synthetic coefficient box has no assay calibration, and the benchmark has only the displayed base input and one displayed refinement. No claim covers unknown thinning, normalization, composition error, shared well noise, hidden types, high-dimensional growth, or uniform post-selection coverage. Under \(M=M_0\), \(G_1=H_1^2/H_2\) and \(G_2=H_2/H_1\).
